mentions.text:
> AI models do not need coherent memory, the access pattern is regular enough that you can make do with explicit barriers.

response to both this and the sibling: even for training, I remember some speculation that explicit synchronization might not even be needed, especially in the middle stages of training (past the early part, before fine tuning). it's not "correct" but the gradient descent will eventually fix it anyway, as long as the error signal doesn't exceed the rate of gradient descent. And "error signal" here isn't just the noise itself but the error in gradient descent caused by incorrect sync - if the average delta in the descent is very slow, so is the amount of error it…
